newsitem.title: USA: Baltimore G&E unit plans Calif. power plant.
newsitem.headline: Baltimore G&E unit plans Calif. power plant.

text.p: A subisidiary of Baltimore Gas and Electric Co, Constellation Power Inc, and Inland Energy Inc, announced Monday plans to construct a 700 megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired power plant near Los Angeles.
The power plant is being configured for peaking and/or combined cycle intermediate load duty and is expected to cost in excess of $250 million.

High Desert Power Project, LLC, a joint venture between Constellation and Inland, a privately-held development company based in Newport Beach, Calif., plans to locate the plant at the former George Air Force Base in Victorville, Calif., just northeast of the Los Angeles basin.
"We can't build anything in the L.A. basin because of the smog...so we are building as nearby as possible," Rick Wolfinger, project manager, said Tuesday.
Groundbreaking for the project is expected in 1999 and commercial operation is planned to begin in 2001.
The project is located at the convergence of several major power transmission lines from the north and east that service the Southern California region.
High Desert Power filed Monday at the California Energy Commission for exemption from certain reviews associated with investor-owned utilities.

Wolfinger explained that under the old regulatory structure new power plants had to undergo prudency reviews, but since the High Desert project is privately owned and will have no effect on ratepayers these requirements are expected to be waived.
High Desert Power plans to submit an application for project certification with the state commission in the second quarter.

"The passage of California Assembly Bill 1890 last August and the opening of the power market by 1998 were critical factors for the company to proceed with the formal waiver and application process," Buck Johns, president of High Desert Power as well as Inland Energy, said in a statement.
"We think we can produce power at a lower price than existing plants in California," said Wolfinger.
